theory.overview: Network flow problems involve finding the maximum flow through a directed graph from a source to a sink, where edges have capacities. The Ford-Fulkerson method (Edmonds-Karp implementation) uses BFS to find augmenting paths. The Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem states that maximum flow equals minimum cut capacity. Applications include bipartite matching, circulation problems, and resource allocation.

keyConcepts.name: Residual Graph
keyConcepts.description: Shows remaining capacity on edges and backward edges for flow cancellation. Augmenting paths found in residual graph.

keyConcepts.name: Augmenting Paths
keyConcepts.description: Path from source to sink in residual graph with available capacity. Bottleneck is minimum residual capacity along path.

keyConcepts.name: Max-Flow Min-Cut
keyConcepts.description: Maximum flow equals minimum cut capacity (sum of capacities of edges crossing a source-sink partition).

keyConcepts.name: Edmonds-Karp
keyConcepts.description: Ford-Fulkerson with BFS for shortest augmenting paths. O(VE²) time. Ensures polynomial time termination.

complexity.dinic: O(V²E) or O(E√V) for unit networks

algorithmSteps.description: Flow network with source S, sink T, capacities on edges
Build residual graph. Forward edges show remaining capacity, backward edges allow flow cancellation
BFS finds augmenting path S→C→D→T with bottleneck capacity 4
Augment 4 units along path. Update residual capacities
Next BFS finds path S→A→B→T with bottleneck 12
Augment 12 units. Total flow now 16. Continue until no augmenting paths

minigame.title: Flow Network Optimizer
minigame.description: Build a flow network and find maximum flow using Ford-Fulkerson. Watch residual graph update dynamically.
